current.jp: えきへの 行き方が わかりません
current.kana: えきえのいきかたがわかりません

structure_explanation.en: Another case of the target pattern 〜方（かた）: 行く (to go) → 行き + 方 = 行き方 (way of going / how to get there). えきへの joins へ (direction, "to") with の, becoming a modifier: えきへの 行き方 = "the way of going to the station". が marks this way as the subject of わかりません (わかる in the polite negative form), "I don't understand / I don't know".
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Mais um caso do padrão-alvo 〜方（かた）: 行く (ir) → 行き + 方 = 行き方 (modo de ir / como chegar). えきへの une へ (direção, "para") com の, virando um modificador: えきへの 行き方 = "o modo de ir para a estação". が marca esse modo como sujeito de わかりません (わかる na forma negativa polida), "não entendo / não sei".

translation_literal.en: I don't know how to get to the station.
translation_literal.pt-BR: O modo de ir para a estação (sujeito), não compreendo.

translation.en: I don't know how to get to the station.
translation.pt-BR: Não sei como chegar à estação.

note.en: 行く in the ます-stem 行き, which joins 方
note.pt-BR: 行く na raiz-ます 行き, que se junta a 方

note.en: suffix 方 (かた) attached to the stem 行き → 行き方 "way of going / how to get there"
note.pt-BR: 接尾辞 方（かた）anexado à raiz 行き → 行き方 "modo de ir / como chegar"

note.en: わかる in the ます-stem わかり, before the negation ません
note.pt-BR: わかる na raiz-ます わかり, antes da negação ません

note.en: ませ, part of ません (polite negative of ます)
note.pt-BR: ませ, parte de ません (negativo polido de ます)

note.en: ん, closes the polite negative わかりません (I don't know / I don't understand)
note.pt-BR: ん, fecha a negação polida わかりません (não sei/não entendo)

objections.objection: Half-applied whitespace cleanup, introduced by this patch. The fix correctly removed the stray spaces from jp ("えきへの 行き方が わかりません" -> "えきへの行き方がわかりません") and dropped the two phantom きごう whitespace tokens, but both explanations still quote the old spaced form: "えきへの 行き方 = 'the way of going to the station'" / "えきへの 行き方 = 'o modo de ir para a estação'". The quoted string no longer matches the jp the learner sees.
objections.auditor_hint: Replace the quoted "えきへの 行き方" with "えきへの行き方" in both locales.

current.jp: この味噌は少し甘いです
current.kana: このみそわすこしあまいです

structure_explanation.en: The topic この味噌 (this miso) is marked by は and functions as the natural subject in pt-BR. Then comes the adverb 少し (a little) modifying the i-adjective 甘い (sweet), and です closes the sentence, giving a polite tone. Note that 甘い already carries the sense of 'is sweet' on its own; です here serves only for politeness, not to conjugate the adjective.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O tópico この味噌 (esse missô) é marcado por は e funciona como sujeito natural em pt-BR. Depois vem o advérbio 少し (um pouco) modificando o adjetivo い 甘い (doce), e です fecha a frase dando tom educado. Note que 甘い já carrega o sentido de 'é doce' sozinho; です aqui serve só para polidez, não para conjugar o adjetivo.

translation_literal.en: This miso is a little sweet.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a esse missô, um pouco doce é (forma polida).

translation.en: This miso is a little sweet.
translation.pt-BR: Esse missô é um pouco doce.

note.en: dictionary form of the i-adjective 甘い (affirmative present)
note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário do adjetivo-い 甘い (presente afirmativo)

note.en: です after an i-adjective only adds the polite register
note.pt-BR: です após adjetivo-い apenas adiciona registro educado

objections.objection: The fix is locale-asymmetric: the op established that この is strictly proximal ('this', never その/あの), and en was corrected everywhere (lit_en 'That miso' -> 'This miso'; tokens[0].gloss.en 'that / this' -> 'this'). But the pt-BR side still glosses この as the medial demonstrative: structure_explanation.pt-BR teaches "この味噌 (esse missô)" and lit_pt reads "Quanto a esse missô", while the same record's tokens[0].gloss.pt-BR now says "este / esta". After the patch the two locales teach different demonstratives for the same word, and the pt-BR explanation contradicts its own token gloss - the very error the op declared major on the en side.
objections.auditor_hint: structure_explanation.pt-BR: "O tópico この味噌 (este missô) ..."; translation_literal.pt-BR: "Quanto a este missô, um pouco doce é (forma polida)."

current.kana: ついたちにおきゅうりょうがはいる

structure_explanation.en: The sentence sets the time with １日に (on the 1st) and has as its subject お給料 (the salary, with the お of politeness) marked by が, ending in the intransitive verb 入る (to come in). 入る here means 'to come in/be deposited (into the account)', something that happens on its own; that is why the subject comes with が. Note the special date reading: １日 is read ついたち. The focus is the vocabulary 給料 (salary).
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase situa o tempo com １日に (no dia 1) e tem como sujeito お給料 (o salário, com o お de polidez) marcado por が, fechando no verbo intransitivo 入る (entrar). 入る aqui significa 'entrar/cair (na conta)', algo que acontece por si; por isso o sujeito vem com が. Repare na leitura especial de data: １日 se lê ついたち. O foco é o vocabulário 給料 (salário).

translation_literal.en: On the 1st, the salary comes in.

translation.en: My salary comes in on the 1st.

role.en: time noun (part of the date: the 1st)
role.pt-BR: substantivo de tempo (parte da data: dia 1)

note.en: dictionary form of 入る (はいる), intransitive verb, present/future
note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário de 入る (はいる), verbo intransitivo, presente/futuro

objections.objection: The fix distributes the fused date reading ついたち across two tokens as １=つい and 日=たち. 日 has no reading たち in any context, so per-token furigana now teaches a false Layer-A fact, and neither token carries a note warning about it (both notes remain null). The op's stated justification ('the merge the hint asks for is impossible here — tokens cannot be added or removed') is contradicted by the bank itself: corpus/sentences/bank.json already stores １日 as a SINGLE token read ついたち in at least four sibling records (来月の１日に会いましょう, 九月の１日は日曜日だ, ４月の１日に学校が始まる, 毎月１日に掃除をする), and 夢のような一日だった likewise stores 一日 -> ついたち as one token. The sentence-level kana (ついたちにおきゅうりょうがはいる), romaji (tsuitachiniokyuuryougahairu) and the new bilingual explanation note are all correct and should be kept; only the token split needs correcting.
objections.auditor_hint: Merge tokens[0]+tokens[1] into a single token １日 with reading ついたち, matching the four sibling records in bank.json. If the pipeline genuinely cannot merge tokens, then at minimum add a note to both tokens stating that ついたち is a fused (熟字訓) reading of １日 and that 日 alone is not read たち.

current.jp: 研究室のドアが開いている
current.kana: けんきゅうしつのどあがあいている

structure_explanation.en: The structure is [noun の noun が verb-ている]. 開く means 'to open(self)' and, in the ている form, describes a continuous state resulting from the action: the door is not opening now, it has already opened and remains open. The が marks ドア (the door) as the subject that entered that state.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A estrutura é [substantivo の substantivo が verbo-ている]. O 開く significa 'abrir(-se)' e, na forma ている, descreve um ESTADO contínuo resultante da ação: a porta não está abrindo agora, ela já se abriu e permanece aberta. O が marca ドア (a porta) como sujeito que entrou nesse estado.

translation_literal.en: As for the research lab's door, it is (in the state of) open.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto à porta do laboratório de pesquisa, ela está (no estado de) aberta.

translation.en: The door to the research lab is open.
translation.pt-BR: A porta do laboratório de pesquisa está aberta.

note.en: て-form of 開く (開いて), used with いる to form the continuous state
note.pt-BR: forma て de 開く (開いて), usada com いる para formar o estado contínuo

note.en: auxiliary いる of 〜ている, indicating a resultant state
note.pt-BR: いる auxiliar de 〜ている, indicando estado resultante

objections.objection: The reading fix (ひらい→あい) is correct, but the after state still ships the topic device on a が-marked subject: 'As for the research lab's door...' / 'Quanto à porta do laboratório de pesquisa...' while the sentence is 研究室のドアが開いている with no は anywhere. The record's own structure_explanation says が marks ドア as the subject, so the literal mirror contradicts the explanation it sits next to. Together with b13ed94a92de these are the only two remaining が+topic-device violations in the batch; every other instance was corrected, so leaving these two is an avoidable inconsistency in a field whose entire purpose is teaching the は/が split.
objections.auditor_hint: en: "The research lab's door (subject), it is (in the state of) open."  |  pt-BR: "A porta do laboratório de pesquisa (sujeito), está (no estado de) aberta."

current.jp: 服が泥で汚れてしまった
current.kana: ふくがどろでよごれてしまった

structure_explanation.en: が marks 服 (clothes) as the subject of what happened. で indicates the cause/means: mud (泥) is what dirtied the clothes. The verb 汚れる (to get dirty) appears in the te-form linked to しまう, and the set 〜てしまった expresses that something happened completely, often with a tone of pity or of something unwanted, translated by 'end up' + gerund.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: が marca 服 (roupa) como o sujeito daquilo que aconteceu. で indica a causa/meio: a lama (泥) é o que sujou a roupa. O verbo 汚れる (ficar sujo) aparece na forma て ligada a しまう, e o conjunto 〜てしまった expressa que algo aconteceu por completo, muitas vezes com tom de pena ou de algo indesejado, traduzido por 'acabar' + gerúndio.

translation_literal.en: As for the clothes (subject), with mud (means), they got dirty (ended up so, past).
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto à roupa (sujeito), com lama (meio), sujou-se (acabou fazendo, passado).

translation.en: My clothes ended up all covered in mud.
translation.pt-BR: A roupa acabou ficando toda suja de lama.

note.en: 汚れる (ichidan, intransitive verb) in the て-form: 汚れて
note.pt-BR: 汚れる (verbo ichidan, intransitivo) na forma て: 汚れて

gloss.en: (to end up doing / to do completely)

note.en: しまう in the past form しまった; 〜てしまった = completed action, with a nuance of regret
note.pt-BR: しまう na forma passada しまった; 〜てしまった = ação completada, com nuance de pena

note.en: た closes しまう in the past: しまった
note.pt-BR: た encerra しまう no passado: しまった

objections.objection: The op edited this exact string (crase fix only) and left the topic-mirror device attached to a が-marked subject. 服が is the subject; the batch's own rule reserves 'Quanto a X / As for X' for the topic particle は. The result is self-contradictory inside one string: 'Quanto à roupa (sujeito)' simultaneously says 'as for the clothes' (topic) and labels it 'sujeito'. lit_en has the identical defect ('As for the clothes (subject)'). This is the same defect class that this very batch fixes as major in eight other records (ac8c3eeccea9, ae0d479e5559, afc2b20beefe, b3f0ef0078d7, b41221ad5c87, b49db2c89280, b4debe07cd5d, b5c5f20e6a99, b71e771c5134), so shipping it leaves the corpus teaching が as a topic marker and the batch internally inconsistent.
objections.auditor_hint: pt-BR: "A roupa (sujeito), com lama (meio), sujou-se (acabou ficando assim, passado)."  |  en: "The clothes (subject), with mud (means), got dirty (ended up so, past)."
